issues.description: Class name and file contents mismatch: the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares/contains a class named 'AnimalFarm' with duplicated package/class declarations and malformed nested code (lines 1-46 of the template). The problem statement UML and description require a class named 'Farm' with a List<Animal> and methods addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), etc. The solution repository provides src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declaring 'public class Farm' (signature at solution line 6) and implementing the expected attributes and methods. The malformed template (wrong identifier and embedded duplicate declarations) will cause compilation errors and prevents students from implementing or testing the intended Farm API.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a correctly named and syntactically valid Farm class that matches the UML and solution. At minimum declare 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' followed by 'public class Farm {', include the field 'private List<Animal> animals;', provide a no-argument constructor that initializes 'animals = new ArrayList<>();', implement public methods 'public List<Animal> getAnimals()', 'public void setAnimals(List<Animal>)', 'public void addAnimal(Animal)', 'public void feedAllAnimals()' (iterating animals and printing a.messageOnFeed()), and 'public void singFarmSong()' which iterates animals and calls a private helper 'private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal)' that prints the verse using animal.getClass().getSimpleName() and animal.messageOnFeed(). Remove any duplicated 'package' or nested 'public class' declarations and stray code inside methods so the file compiles and exposes the intended API for students to complete.

issues.description: The concept 'Farm' (the class representing the collection of animals) is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the solution repository define a public class named 'Farm', but the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named 'AnimalFarm'. Because the filename is Farm.java, the public class name must be Farm; the mismatch will prevent compilation and blocks students from mapping the exercise tasks (which refer to class 'Farm' and methods like addAnimal, singFarmSong) to the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: In src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java (template), rename the public class declaration from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' so the public class name matches the filename and the problem statement/solution. Ensure the class signature is 'public class Farm { ... }' and implement the expected methods/fields (addAnimal, singFarmSong, animals list) or leave TODOs consistent with the 'Farm' identifier.
